item.title: Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: O brahmin, striving, cut the stream, Abandon and…
item.description:
Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

O brahmin, striving, cut the stream,
Abandon and destroy
All clinging to sensual desires.
Without cutting sensual desires,
A sage cannot attain unification of mind.
If you do what should be done,
Be steadfast and energetic.
If a goer-forth is lazy,
He scatters even more dust.
Not doing is better than doing badly —
Doing badly leads to suffering afterward.
Having done, do it well —
Doing well brings no suffering.
Like holding grass the wrong way,
It can cut your hand,
So too, the ascetic life wrongly practiced
Drags one to hell.
Any lazy conduct,
Any defiled practice,
Any evil action in the holy life
Does not yield great fruit.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.8

item.title: “Monks, I do not see any other fetter by which beings, fettered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this fetter of craving. Monks,…
item.description:
“Monks, I do not see any other fetter by which beings, fettered, wander and transmigrate for a long time as this fetter of craving. Monks, fettered by the fetter of craving, beings wander and transmigrate for a long time.

One with craving as companion
Wanders on for a long time.
Neither here nor there beyond such becoming
Can they cross the wandering.

Knowing this peril — that craving
Is the origin of suffering —
Free from craving, without clinging,
Mindful, the monk lives the homeless life.”

From: Itivuttaka 15
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or…
item.description:
“And what, monks, is the peril in the case of forms? Here, monks, one might see that woman at another time — eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old — aged, bent like a roof, crooked, leaning on a staff, trembling as she walks, sick, her youth exhausted, teeth broken, hair grey, bald, wrinkled, limbs shriveled and pale. What do you think, monks? Has her former charm and beauty disappeared and peril become evident?” “Yes, venerable sir.” “Thus, monks, is the peril in the case of forms.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, just as a defiled, dusty cloth, if placed in clean water becomes clean, if placed in a furnace becomes clean. So too, monks, a…
item.description:
“Monks, just as a defiled, dusty cloth, if placed in clean water becomes clean, if placed in a furnace becomes clean. So too, monks, a monk of such virtue, such quality, such wisdom – even if he eats almsfood of choice rice with black grains removed, various soups and curries – that does not become an obstacle for him.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 7 – Vatthūpamasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Dependent on attachment, suffering arises. All the various sufferings in the world Come into being through attachment. The fool, by making attachments, Again and again…
item.description:
“Dependent on attachment, suffering arises.
All the various sufferings in the world
Come into being through attachment.
The fool, by making attachments,
Again and again encounters suffering.
Therefore, the wise one, knowing,
Does not create attachments,
Contemplating the nature of birth and suffering.

Those who fall into the stream
Of repeated birth and death,
Going from one existence to another,
Are deluded by ignorance.

This great delusion, ignorance,
Leads to long wandering —
But beings who have attained true knowledge
Do not go to renewed existence.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 3.12
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: One with craving as companion Wanders for a long time — Now here, now there — He cannot stop The wandering of rebirth. Having understood…
item.description:
One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time —
Now here, now there —
He cannot stop
The wandering of rebirth.
Having understood this danger —
That craving is the origin of suffering —
The monk, abandoning craving,
Not grasping, not clinging,
Mindfully dwells,
Living the homeless life.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.9
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Udāyi, here some foolish person, when I say ‘Abandon this,’ says: ‘What is this trivial, petty thing? This ascetic is too strict about this restraint…
item.description:
“Udāyi, here some foolish person, when I say ‘Abandon this,’ says: ‘What is this trivial, petty thing? This ascetic is too strict about this restraint and elimination.’ They do not abandon it and they create discontent against me and against the monks who wish to train in the precepts. That, Udāyi, becomes for them a strong bond, a firm bond, a sturdy bond, a rotting not-less bond, a great log.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta

item.title: “Then, while the Venerable Udāyi was in solitary retreat, this thought arose in his mind: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many painful states for…
item.description:
“Then, while the Venerable Udāyi was in solitary retreat, this thought arose in his mind: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many painful states for us. Indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many pleasant states. Indeed, the Blessed One has abandoned many unwholesome states for us. Indeed, the Blessed One has brought us many wholesome states.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 66 – Laṭukikopamasutta

item.title: Venerable Ajita: “By what is the world shrouded? Why does it not shine forth? What do you call its defilement? What is its great fear?”…
item.description:
Venerable Ajita:
“By what is the world shrouded?
Why does it not shine forth?
What do you call its defilement?
What is its great fear?”

The Blessed One:
“The world is shrouded by ignorance.
Through stinginess and heedlessness it does not shine forth.
I say longing is its defilement —
Suffering is its great fear.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 5.2

item.title: “If there were no gratification in form, monks, beings would not become lustful for form. But because there is gratification in form, beings become lustful…
item.description:
“If there were no gratification in form, monks, beings would not become lustful for form. But because there is gratification in form, beings become lustful for form. If there were no peril in form, beings would not become disenchanted with form. But because there is peril in form, beings become disenchanted with form. If there were no escape from form, beings would not escape from form. But because there is escape from form, beings escape from form. Monks, as long as beings do not directly know as it actually is the gratification as gratification, the peril as peril, the escape as escape in regard to these six internal sense bases, they have not, monks, along with this world of devas, Māras, Brahmās, with its ascetics and brahmins, with its devas and humans, dwelt with minds free from clinging, detached, liberated, unbounded. But because beings have directly known them as they actually are, therefore they have dwelt with minds free from clinging, detached, liberated, unbounded.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.18
